findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The dependents list leaves out the shared fake planner and the CLI integration tests. Those jobs would now run real cargo, and the test seam cannot reach them.
findings.evidence: The shared fake planner gives every criterion a demonstration with command "cargo test --locked" and a non-blank fails_without (fake.rs:366-368). CLI integration tests that run planned jobs with fake agents also build plans like this: lifecycle.rs:2647-2650, introspection.rs:742-746, job_plan.rs:410-416. In run/tests.rs, behavior_plan (tests.rs:668-678) uses the same command, and the existing test at tests.rs:861 lands a job with it. Once this change lands, all of these jobs will run real `cargo test --locked` in a scratch copy of their fixture repository before the verifier starts. A #[cfg(test)] seam in athena-core is not compiled into the athena-cli integration tests. The plan's dependents list says only that jobs with no plan are unchanged. Fix: Add these readers to the dependents list, each with the test that covers it. Decide what the stage does for these callers and test that outcome. One option: expose the seam like ci_seam, under #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))], so the fake setup can install it. Another: have the fake planner emit no fails_without. Either way, state the effect on the brief text those tests read (job_plan.rs:345-348) and on their running time.
findings.location: Dependents list; Decision 9 (demo_seam is #[cfg(test)] in run/checks.rs); crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:354-368

findings.summary: When the revert drops the parent's declaration of a new test file, its tests disappear without the record saying so.
findings.evidence: The repository declares test modules without a body in non-test files: lib.rs:108-109 `#[cfg(test)] mod run_pin_tests;`, gh/mod.rs:109-110 and athena-gate/src/lib.rs:387-388. Scan records only modules that have a body (code_health.rs:111-119). Suppose a candidate adds a new `*_tests.rs` file. The file is kept, but reverting its parent removes the declaration, so the new tests are never compiled. The run then reports 'ran no tests', and tests_removed does not name the file. This contradicts Decision 2. Fix: Also carry over the candidate's `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` declarations when reverting a file, or list the orphaned test file in tests_removed. Add a unit test for this case.

findings.summary: Identical demonstration commands are run more than once.
findings.evidence: Planners often use `cargo test --locked` for several criteria; the fake planner and lifecycle.rs both do. The plan would run the same full suite up to 3 times on the same reverted tree. Fix: Run each distinct command once and attach its record to every criterion that names it.

findings.summary: code_health.rs is outside the listed deliverables. This is Athena's own finding, weighed here.
findings.evidence: Reusing Scan is a sound reason to touch the file, but the scope check will flag it. Fix: Keep the change and justify it in the change description as reuse of the single definition of a test module.
base_script is defined at run/tests.rs:215, not line 250. Fix: Correct the line reference.

summary: The plan reads the request correctly and puts the fix in the right place: a new stage in verification_stage, run before the disk gate, adds 'not a check' entries to inputs.checks and leaves check_runs and judge untouched. It also answers the round-1 findings. The revert keeps inline tests by reusing Scan, results are classified from tests_ran rather than the clipped tail, and the scratch copy is always removed, following take_baseline. I confirmed the named code exists: verifier_snapshot (verification.rs:405), the 'not a check' entries (verification.rs:88-127), take_baseline and baseline_checks (checks.rs:92-159), run_check (checks.rs:424-540) and Scan (code_health.rs:87-123). The demonstrations for criteria 1-3 cover their criteria and would fail without the change. One major gap remains. The shared fake planner (fake.rs:366-368) and several CLI integration fixtures plan `cargo test --locked` with a fails_without. With this change those jobs would run real cargo in scratch copies, a #[cfg(test)] seam cannot reach the CLI integration tests, and the dependents list omits these callers. Smaller issues: test-module declarations without a body are dropped silently, identical commands are not deduplicated, and code_health.rs is outside the deliverables. Verdict: revise.
